guideposts.label: Welcome (back) to Granada
guideposts.detail: La Vuelta 26 returns to the province of Granada (previously home to stage 13) for the final week-end. For the first time in the race history, all the Andalusian provinces hosted at least one stage in its entirety: Almeria (stage 12), Jaen (stage 14), Cordoba (15), Huelva (16), Seville (17), Cadiz (18), and Malaga (19). Both La Calahorra and Collado del Alguacil make their debuts as La Vuelta stage

guideposts.label: A familiar area, especially for Carlos Rodriguez
guideposts.detail: Most riders are familiar with the area, either thanks to the many races organised around Granada, or from the training camps teams and riders are used to hold in the Sierra Nevada. Carlos Rodriguez (Netcompany Ineos) is the local rider of the day, hailing from Almuñecar in the province of Granada. His hometown hosted the start of stage 13 a week ago.

guideposts.label: La Roja
guideposts.detail: Despite the attacks launched by Richard Carrapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), the top GC contenders finished together yesterday at Peñas Blancas. Enric Mas (Movistar), the overall leader since stage 8, enters the final week-end with a lead of 1’37’’ over Roglic. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) follows with a gap of 3’01’’, and Carapaz trails by 5’17’’. Oscar

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Eddie Dunbar (1st), Thomas Gloag (3rd) and Marcel Camprubi (5th) dominating the climb up Peñas Blancas, Pinarello Q36.5 had the strongest collective performance yesterday. Decathlon CMA CGM still lead the overall team standings with a gap of 58’06’’ to XDS Astana and 1h09’36’’ to Groupama-FDJ United.

guideposts.label: Van Aert and Oliveira keep pushing
guideposts.detail: The duo are half a minute ahead of the bunch after 13 kilometres.

guideposts.label: Mas is caught behind
guideposts.detail: His Movistar teammates in the first peloton drop back to drive the chase for the wearer of La Roja.

guideposts.label: The bunches get back together
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, there's a group of chasers featuring six Uno-X Mobility riders 15 seconds behind the leading duo, who have covered 25 kilometres.

guideposts.label: Movistar on the counter-attack
guideposts.detail: Raul Garcia Pierna and Ivan Romeo (Movistar) set off from the bunch with Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and James Shaw (EF Education-EasyPost). At km 35, they are 25 seconds behind the 14 leaders.

guideposts.label: The battle goes on after almost 40 kilometres of hard racing
guideposts.detail: The fourteen leaders don't look behind. The four chasers were joined by a fez dozens more, but Enric Mas (Movistar) and his teammates reacted to regroup the bunch.

guideposts.label: Crash in the first positions of the peloton
guideposts.detail: Matthew Riccitello (Decathlon CMA CGM) rapidly got back up but Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL) was in much more pain.

guideposts.label: Riccitello abandons after his crash
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, the battle goes on with a group of 27 chasers between the 14 leaders and the peloton (+50'').

guideposts.label: 49.2 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: That's a brutal pace on rolling terrain... And the battle goes on!

guideposts.label: The situation at km 58
guideposts.detail: The same 14 attackerslead the way on the downhill. A massive chase group has emerged a minute behind. The gap to the bunch has increased to over 3 minutes.

guideposts.label: The gaps increase on the valley
guideposts.detail: The 14 leaders have covered 81 km. The chasers trail by 3'10''. The peloton are 8'25'' behind.

guideposts.label: Carapaz, inspired again by the Puerto de El Purche?
guideposts.detail: Collado del Alguacil is in the municipality of Güejar Sierra, like Alto de Hazallanas. This climb made its debut in La Vuelta 13 (Chris Horner won the stage and took La Roja form Vincenzo Nibali) and was at the heart of stage 9 in La Vuelta 24, with two ascents up Alto de Hazallanas before finishing in Granada. Part of the breakaway, Adam Yates attacked on these slopes, and covered the last 57 kil

guideposts.label: The chasers begin the ascent
guideposts.detail: They trail by three and a half minutes at the bottom. Meanwhile, the gap to the peloton increases to 10'30''.

guideposts.label: Martin-Guyonnet enters the virtual GC top 10
guideposts.detail: There is now a gap of 8 minutes between the chasers and the peloton. At the start of the stage, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United) was 7'52'' behind Harold Tejada (XDS Astana), 10th in the overall standings. He needs 9'13'' to catch Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek).

guideposts.label: Sepp Kuss attacks from the bunch
guideposts.detail: The American climber has a massive gap to close. But he's likely to receive support from teammates who can drop from the chasing group. Armirail, Brennan, Kruijswijk and Nordhagen are all there.

guideposts.label: The leaders face the final 3 km of ascent
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) has opened a 25'' gap to the bunch.

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks with 99 km to go
guideposts.detail: Decathlon CMA CGM take over the pace-setting in the bunch.

guideposts.label: Carapaz joins Kuss
guideposts.detail: They are 35 seconds ahead of the bunch. Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) struggles.

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto de El Purche (cat. 1, km 94.3)
guideposts.detail: 1. Van Aert, 10 pts 2. Miquel, 6 pts 3. Leknessund, 4 pts 4. Chamberlain, 2 pts 5. Cort, 1 pt

guideposts.label: The leaders maketheir way to the second ascent of Puerto de El Purche
guideposts.detail: +2'40'' Chase group +8'35'' Mas group +9'10'' Onley group

guideposts.label: 4 chasers 2'30'' behind the leaders
guideposts.detail: This group is made of Walter Calzoni (Pinarello Q36.5), Lucas Hamilton (Netcompany Ineos), Mikel Landa (Soudal Quick-Step), and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma).

guideposts.label: The gap from the Mas group to the Onley group has significantly increased
guideposts.detail: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) and his companions are three and a half minutes behind Enric Mas (Movistar).

guideposts.label: Kuss attacks the GC group
guideposts.detail: The American is around 5 kilometres from the summit. De Pestel sets the pace in the group.

guideposts.label: Van Aert takes 10 more KOM points
guideposts.detail: The Belgian is now 16 points behind Buitrago. There are 10 points for the first rider at Puerto de El Duque, and 20 for the winner of the stage.

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks again
guideposts.detail: Gall immediately reacts, followed by Mas and Roglic.

guideposts.label: Landa joins the leading group
guideposts.detail: They are on the downhill, 55 kilometres from the finish.

guideposts.label: Results at the Puerto de El Purche (cat. 1, km 125.5)
guideposts.detail: 1. Van Aert, 10 pts 2. Miquel, 6 pts 3. Leknessund, 4 pts 4. Chamberlain, 2 pts 5. Kron, 1 pt

guideposts.label: Carapaz is caught by Gall, Mas and Roglic
guideposts.detail: They are 7'20'' behind the leaders, and 50'' behind Kuss.

guideposts.label: 50 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The leaders are headed to the intermediate sprint. If Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) scores points there, he will be mathematically out of reach from anyone.

guideposts.label: Richard Carapaz accelerates on the downhill
guideposts.detail: The GC contenders are 7'30'' behind the leaders. Oscar Chamberlain is dropped from the breakaway. Is he waiting for Felix Gall?

guideposts.label: Kuss is 2 minutes ahead of the Mas group
guideposts.detail: He is 6 minutes behind the leaders.

guideposts.label: 45 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Van Aert is about to seal the deal for the green jersey at the intermediate sprint. Debruyne is 40'' behind the leaders. Then, the chasing group trail by 1'25''. In the GC group, Garcia Pierna sets the pace for Mas two minutes behind Kuss and 8 minutes behind the leaders.

guideposts.label: Debruyne accelerates with 38 km to go
guideposts.detail: The Belgian youngster is followed by Johannessen and Landa.

guideposts.label: Roglic sets the pace in the GC group
guideposts.detail: He's dollowed by Mas, Gall, Carapaz, Rodriguez and Gogl.

guideposts.label: Johannessen, Landa and Debruyne are 3 km from the summit
guideposts.detail: +1'35'' Chaser group +5' Kuss +8' Mas group

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks (again!)
guideposts.detail: Gall, Roglic and Mas manage to follow the Ecuadorian climber.

guideposts.label: Carapaz has another go
guideposts.detail: But Gall, Mas and Roglic still keep up with the pace by the Ecuadorian climber.

guideposts.label: Landa leads the way to the summit
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard collaborated with Johannessen and Debruyne up the Puerto de El Duque.

guideposts.label: The pace drops in the GC group
guideposts.detail: After a few unsuccessful attacks, it's Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step) who currently sets the pace, followed by Mas, Armirail, Roglic, Carapaz, JF Rodriguez and Gall.

guideposts.label: The average speed after four hours: 39.5 km/h
guideposts.detail: The leaders are 28 kilometres from the finish. Miquel trails by 30 seconds.

guideposts.label: And another attack by Carapaz
guideposts.detail: Gall, Mas and Roglic still follow.

guideposts.label: Carapaz tries again and again
guideposts.detail: But he is not finding an opening.

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto de El Duque (cat. 1, km 155.4)
guideposts.detail: 1. Landa, 10 pts / 6'' 2. Debruyne, 6 pts / 4'' 3. Johannessen, 4 pts 4. Miquel, 2pts 5. Widar, 1pt

guideposts.label: 20 kilometres to go for the leading trio
guideposts.detail: The final ascent begins with 8.3 km to go.

guideposts.label: Collado del Alguacil, a new summit in professional cycling
guideposts.detail: The Collado del Alguacil climb is an unprecedented climb in the world of professional cycling that was, according to Luis Angel Maté’s account, discovered by the late Xavi Tondo. Hailing from Tarragona (Catalonia), Tondo used to train in Sierra Nevada with his coach Francis Cabello (11 participations in La Vuelta between 1990 and 2004, 1 stage win in the Tour de France) and was keen to explore new

guideposts.label: The gaps as the lead trio are 14 km from the finish
guideposts.detail: +35’’ Miquel +2’10’’ Nordhagen, Hirt, Widar, Berrade +4’25’’ Van Aert, Kuss +9’45’’ Mas group

guideposts.label: Kuss is moving in the GC top 5 and threatening Carapaz
guideposts.detail: The American climber is currently riding 5'25'' ahead of the Mas group. He started the day 5'47'' behind Carapaz on GC.

guideposts.label: The Kuss group are 3 minutes behind the leaders
guideposts.detail: Van Aert sets the pace at the bottom of the climb, followed by Nordhagen, Kuss, Calzoni, Fortunato, Berrade and Widar.

guideposts.label: Landa vs Johannessen
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard leads by 23 seconds as he tackles the final 4 kilometres. Debruyne trails by 55''. The Kuss group are 5 km from the summit.

guideposts.label: Gall attacks
guideposts.detail: Mas follows him. Roglic chases.

guideposts.label: Gall drops Mas
guideposts.detail: The Spanish wearrer of La Roja loses a few metres. Roglic is 25 seconds behind.

guideposts.label: Gall opens gaps
guideposts.detail: +10'' Mas +40'' Roglic +1'10'' Carapaz

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Mikel Landa (Soudal Quick-Step) 2. Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility), +47’’ 3. Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech), +1’27’’ 4. Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious), +3’00’’ 5. Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma), +4’&3’’
